text:
Andrew Copp is playing more than 18 minutes a night on a Red Wings team that has run out of centers it can count on, with Dylan Larkin suspended while he waits for a trade. That's a lot to ask of a role player, and it shows: Detroit has 49% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, five points worse than without him.

The production (8 points in 19 games, half on the power play) is about what the chances say, a touch under. Last season was kinder to him than it should have been; Evolving-Hockey noted his results ran ahead of his chances (1.3 wins against -0.6 expected). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still credits him with clean exits and lots of shot assists.

The Ann Arbor native is a useful player being asked to be more than that. Our range for his season: 35 to 55 points.
